title: observability: token/KV tracing + dashboards + alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds token-level KV-cache metrics and tracing spans, new Grafana dashboards for token/cost/latency breakdowns, and tuned alerts to reduce noise while preserving SLO coverage.
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token cost, KV cache hit behavior, and end-to-end request tracing to diagnose regressions in latency and cost. This PR introduces token-level KV cache metrics, propagates tracing spans through the KV layer, ships updated Grafana dashboards with cost/latency breakdowns, and adjusts alert thresholds to reduce false positives seen during batch spikes.

What this changes (high level):
- Emit token-level metrics for requests (token_count, token_cost_estimate, token_latency) and KV-specific metrics (kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_latency_ms) with the same labels we use for model & route attribution.
- Add tracing spans around KV cache lookup/insert to link cache behavior to upstream latency. Spans include kv.key_hash (redacted) and hit/miss tag.
- New Grafana dashboard: Observability / Token & KV Cost-Latency (prefab panels for cost per token, latency distribution, KV hit-rate by model).
- Alert tuning: move from absolute rate alerts to anomaly-based thresholds using median-based windows, add suppressions for planned rollouts, and widen SLO burn-rate windows to reduce churn during transient batch events.
- Backfill and migration: provide a short adaptor to map existing aggregate metrics to the new token-level labels for dashboards to render historical views.

Checklist: 
- [x] Emit metrics from runtime and worker processes
- [x] Add tracing spans in KV code path
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and provisioning updates
- [x] Alert rule changes and runbook updates
- [x] Add integration tests for metric emission and trace correlation
- [x] Docs update for Observability guide (docs/observability/token-kv.md)

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (token-level observability epic), SRE-211 (alert noise reduction). See linked dashboard PR in infra (infra#4213) for provisioning changes.

Notes on rollout: We gated metric emission behind a feature flag observed_token_metrics=true to allow progressive rollout to Dedicated clusters and avoid immediate high-cardinality exposure on small customers. Default behavior remains unchanged for older clusters until the flag is enabled.

Risks and mitigations: New metrics increase cardinality. Mitigations: feature-flag rollout, sampling option for high-throughput routes, and aggregation knobs in Prometheus remote write. Alert tuning tested on staging and observed with synthetic load for 72 hours before merge.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Could we avoid exposing raw KV keys in spans? Please ensure we only emit hashed/redacted identifiers and confirm GDPR-safe behavior.
Aisha Patel: Agree - using a salted hash. Updated kv_tracing.go to redact and add a note in docs about hashing parameters.
Sofia Martinez: The new alert for 'kv_miss_rate' fires a lot in staging during bulk imports. Can we add a 10m suppression window for route=ingest?
Aisha Patel: Added route-level suppression and widened the anomaly window. Also added a runbook section for ingest-batch scenarios.

Devon Brooks: Metrics look good; minor nit: prefer histogram for kv_latency_ms rather than gauge to get quantiles.\n\nAisha Patel: Switched to histogram buckets and updated dashboard panels to use histogram_quantile for p50/p95.
Liam Chen: CI flaky test 'TestTelemetryEmission' failed once; reran and it passed. Please monitor post-merge.\n\nAisha Patel: Added retry/backoff in test harness and increased wait timeout.

Monitor token_metric_ingestion and cost_per_token dashboards for 48h (sre)
Coordinate with Dedicated onboarding for flag rollout (solutions)
Follow up: reduce sampling rate if Prometheus remote write ingress > 20% (infra)
